motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing items 12.C. and 12.D. from the agenda and placing them after Item 13.A. on the regular agenda. Councilmember Rich Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Routine items approved; two pulled for debate
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote, but pulled the downtown plan and inland port resolutions out to be discussed separately later that night.
motions.impact: This is procedural housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It only meant the downtown plan and inland port items each got their own discussion instead of passing without one.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Enyo Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Enyo Development Agreement as presented in the agenda packet. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development agreement with Enyo
motions.summary: The council took up an ordinance approving a development agreement with Enyo, with the terms set out in the meeting packet rather than in the motion itself.
motions.impact: The motion gives no details, so there is nothing here that tells you what Enyo would build, where, or when. The specifics live in the agenda packet.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Downtown Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt the Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Adopting the Downtown Master Plan. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Downtown master plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted the Downtown Master Plan, the city's guiding document for how Eagle Mountain's downtown area should develop.
motions.impact: You won't see anything change on the ground yet. The plan is the blueprint the city will measure future downtown projects against, so it shapes what gets built there over time.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table the Resolution, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City, for further discussion. Councilmember Rich Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Inland port proposal put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside a resolution supporting a Utah Inland Port Authority project area in Eagle Mountain, holding it for further discussion at a later meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing is settled — no port area is created for now. If you have a view on an inland port in Eagle Mountain, the item is still open and will come back to the council.
